newsitem.title: UK: Entrepreneur Goldsmith critical with cancer - papers.
newsitem.headline: Entrepreneur Goldsmith critical with cancer - papers.

text.p: Anglo-French entrepreneur Sir James Goldsmith is critically ill with cancer in a hospital near Paris, British newspapers reported on Monday.
The Times said members of Goldsmith's family, including his daughter Jemima, wife of former Pakistan cricket captain Imran Khan, had gathered at his bedside.

Goldsmith, 64, first suffered pancreatic cancer in 1985 but its recurrence was kept secret when he led his Referendum Party in the six-week campaign for Britain's May 1 general election, the newspaper said.
The party campaigned against further European Union integration but failed to win a seat in the election, which resulted in a landslide victory for Tony Blair's Labour Party.
The Times quoted friends of Goldsmith as saying they were concerned about his condition.
"I think it is very bad. He is a hero. He fought that (election) campaign, having confided in only a handful of people, despite the most chronic pains," said one unidentified friend.
Reuters was unable to confirm the reports early on Monday.
Goldsmith masterminded million-dollar Wall Street deals and made a vast fortune as one of the most cool and astute corporate raiders of his time.
He amassed millions by buying into companies and then selling the stock for big profits after takeover speculation had boosted share prices.
